newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission "takes note" of Yeltsin's Europe bid.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission "takes note" of Yeltsin's Europe bid.

text.p: The European Commission, the executive body of the European Union, said on Saturday it "takes note" of a statement by Russian President Boris Yeltsin that his country wants to join the EU.

"We take note of Russian President Yeltsin's declaration. One should be reminded that we do have a partnership and cooperation agreement which was signed in Corfu the 24th of June 1994. It has not been ratified yet, but our relations are based on that," a Commission spokesman told Reuters. He declined further comment.
The spokesman said Yeltsin's statement may be discussed at an EU Foreign Ministers meeting on Monday.

"(Russia) is aiming to be recognised finally as a full European state and we are also prepared to join the European Union," Yeltsin told reporters in Helsinki on Saturday, a day after his summit meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton.

The EU-Russia partnership and cooperation agreement is designed to forge commercial and other links and to liberalise trade. But the deal has not been fully ratified and Moscow has not formally applied to join the 15-nation EU bloc.
Since the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989, the EU has had a twin-track approach to the former communist world, roughly differentiating between former Soviet republics and independent countries.
Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Romania, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania have all been promised eventual EU membership.
Formal membership negotiations with at least some of the countries will begin early next year. Poland, the Czech republic, Hungary and possibly Slovenia are expected to be the first to join.
Russia itself along with former republics such as Ukraine and Belarus, have not been promised membership, but have negotiated special trade and political cooperation agreements.
In Moscow's case, as the partnership and cooperation agreement has not yet been fully ratified by either side, relations are conducted under an interim agreement.
